sections.heading: C2 — Driver licensing
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Driver licensing

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may travel for a job, employment or farm work. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may take the direct home-school route on school days for attendance, excluding school activities. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may travel directly to or from an activity held by a religious organization. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may drive when a licensed adult sits in front. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A13
Restricted-license drivers aged 15 may not carry minors who are not siblings. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver may use a wireless device only for reporting unlawful activity or summoning emergency help. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive for school and approved school activities. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may travel directly to or from a religious organization's activity. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive for work, employment or farm duties. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive while accompanied by a licensed adult in front. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A13
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may carry only one minor passenger who is not a sibling. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A13
After reaching 16 and holding a restricted license for 6 months, the listed age restrictions end. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A13
Applicants younger than 18 seeking an unrestricted license need a parent or guardian affidavit confirming at least 50 practice hours. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A13
The unrestricted-license practice affidavit for applicants below 18 must include at least 10 nighttime hours. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A13
An unrestricted-license applicant must pass vision, written and driving tests or supply the specified driver-education completion slip. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A13
License applicants undergo station vision screening or submit an eye-examination form completed by a licensed eye specialist within 90 days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A13
Station vision screening requires at least 20/40 vision in one eye. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A13
Drivers who need corrective lenses to meet the vision standard receive a restriction requiring those lenses whenever driving. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A13
An applicant who fails vision screening must have the licensing eye form completed by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A13
Returning the eye form within 90 days of examination lets licensing staff decide whether to issue a license or require further testing. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A13
The Kansas knowledge exam covers traffic law and sign recognition by shape, color or symbol. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A13
The driving exam uses a designated traffic route to demonstrate basic vehicle-operation skills. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A13
Graduated licensing introduces beginner drivers to more complex situations in stages after initial lower-risk experience. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A14
After a failed written or driving exam, retesting is available on the next working day after payment of the re-exam fee. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A14
The handbook lists a re-examination fee of one dollar and fifty cents. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A14
Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the written exam. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A14
Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the driving exam. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A14
A fourth failure of either exam requires waiting at least 6 months from the latest failure before retesting. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A14
An applicant receives a license only after passing the required exams and meeting the other licensing conditions. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A14
Renewing an instructional permit requires passing the written exam again. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A14
A temporary resident's license, permit or identification card expires when lawful-presence authorization expires. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A14
The Division sends a license-expiration or renewal notice at least 30 days before expiration. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R34 | anchor: A14
Renewal notices use the mailing address on record or the email address selected for electronic notices. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R35 | anchor: A14
Renewal includes vision screening, with a qualifying eye-specialist examination from within 90 days accepted instead. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R36 | anchor: A14
A licensing examiner may require a renewal applicant to take a written or driving test when ordinary vehicle control is in doubt. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R37 | anchor: A14
The handbook lists an additional expired-license penalty of one dollar. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R38 | anchor: A14
A license expired for more than one year requires vision, written and driving testing. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R39 | anchor: A14
A Kansas license may generally be renewed at any state driver-license office regardless of the holder's Kansas residence. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R40 | anchor: A14
Registered offenders must use a full-service station for renewal. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R41 | anchor: A14
A separate-card concealed-carry license holder may renew at any station if no name, address or license-number changes are needed. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R42 | anchor: A14
Three moving-violation convictions within 12 months can cause a license suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R43 | anchor: A14
The handbook lists chemical-test refusal suspensions of one year for a first refusal, two for a second, three for a third and ten for a fourth. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R44 | anchor: A14
Failing to attend a required court date or respond to a traffic citation can produce an indefinite suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R45 | anchor: A14
Failure to keep continuous vehicle liability insurance carries an indefinite suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

Misconceptions: A permit does not authorize unsupervised driving; use the supervision facts rather than treating it as an unrestricted license.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: identify the license path, then its supervisor, passenger and trip conditions; this cue adds no legal rule.
Glossary: Use the fact blocks to distinguish instructional permit, restricted license, farm permit and graduated licensing.
Dynamic facts: Age rules, fees, renewal procedures and sanctions are edition-bound administrative or legal values requiring issuer refresh; contact addresses and office hours are excluded from stable teaching.

sections.heading: C2 — Driver licensing
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Driver licensing

FACT_ID: sec01-R46 | anchor: A14
Impaired driving or an alcohol-test result of .08 or higher can cause suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R47 | anchor: A14
Transporting an open alcoholic-beverage container can cause suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R48 | anchor: A14
Failure to report a traffic crash can cause suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R49 | anchor: A15
A vehicular-homicide conviction can result in revoked driving privileges. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R50 | anchor: A15
A conviction for leaving a crash involving injury or death without stopping and helping can cause revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R51 | anchor: A15
A reckless-driving conviction can cause revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R52 | anchor: A15
Using a vehicle to commit a felony can result in license revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R53 | anchor: A15
A conviction for trying to evade a police officer can cause revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R54 | anchor: A15
Aggravated vehicular homicide can cause license revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R55 | anchor: A15
Vehicular battery can cause license revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R56 | anchor: A15
The handbook states that a fifth alcohol-test result of .08 or higher or chemical-test refusal leads to permanent revocation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R57 | anchor: A15
Nonresident students with a valid license may drive in Kansas if they are at least 16. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R58 | anchor: A15
Active-duty military members and qualifying spouses and children may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R59 | anchor: A15
Temporarily assigned qualifying company trainees or instructors may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R60 | anchor: A15
Foreign tourists, teachers and business visitors staying up to one year may use a valid license from age 16 with valid immigration documents. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R61 | anchor: A15
A nonresident visitor with a valid state license may drive in Kansas from age 16. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0015]
